title: Efficacy of perioperative duloxetine in patients at high risk for developing chronic postsurgical pain after inguinal hernia repair: a multicenter randomized controlled trial
official: Efficacy of perioperative duloxetine in patients at high risk for developing chronic postsurgical pain after inguinal hernia repair: a multicenter randomized controlled trial
summary: Main objective: To determine the efficacy of duloxetine versus placebo in reducing the incidence of CPSP at 4 months in patients at high risk of this complication
conditions: Chronic postsurgical pain after inguinal hernia repair

interventions.name: Dulotex 30 mg cápsulas duras gastrorresistentes EFG

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Men that live in Spain during the entire trial and who are  scheduled for open inguinal hernia repair (inpatient or  outpatient procedures).
2. Risk of post-surgical pain chronification ≥ 16% using the GENDOLCAT risk scale.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Age under 18 years
2. History of liver failure (Child-Pug B or C)
3. Currently taking a monoamine oxidase inhibitor or other  medication with substantial interaction with duloxetine
4. Antidepressant use within 4 weeks of study start
5. Treatment with inhibitors of CYP1A2: fluvoxamine,  ciprofloxacin or enoxacin
6. History of uncontrolled hypertension
7. History of bipolar disorder
8. History of seizures over 18 years of age, not during  chilhood for febrile seizures
9. Clinical record of acute glaucoma
10. Treatment with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors  (SSRIs)
11. Treatment with serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake  inhibitors (SNRIs)
12. Patients who in the recruiter’s opinion have insufficient knowledge of Spanish to understand the trial
13. Treatment with tricyclic antidepressants
14. Treatment with triptans
15. Treatment with antipsychotic drugs
16. Treatment with dopamine antagonists
17. Treatment with oral anticoagulant agents
18. Treatment with St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum)
19. History of Major depression disorder
20. History of Generalized anxiety disorder
21. Patients who are currently being treated with duloxetine
22. Patients with known allergy to duloxetine or  hypersensitivity to any of the excipients
23. Serious renal failure (creatinine clearance >30 ml/min in  blood test during 3 months before surgery)
24. Patients requiring reoperation because of surgical  complications
25. Transplanted patients
26. History of coronary artery disease, including previous  myocardial infarction, angina, percutaneous transluminal  coronary angioplasty
27. History of congestive heart failure
